summary: Stage 3 (helpers, reliability flags, work record) frontend e2e verified end-to-end at desktop 1920x1080 and mobile 390x844. All owner and crew data-testids required by the spec render and wire to the backend correctly. Owner Reliability panel resolves flags via the dialog (short-reason toast rejection + real-reason POST 200 + list refresh), Crew Pool flag badges reflect unresolved counts, Job Timeline dialog surfaces distinct PROBLEM REPORTED and RELIABILITY FLAG entries with data-testid=timeline-label-problem / timeline-label-flag including who/when. Helper flow: my-flags-strip appears only when they have their own non-resolved flags (never any other crew's — verified 'Stage2 Tester' string absent), Dispute dialog rejects <3-char reasons and on success updates the row to 'Disputed — waiting on the owner'. Report-a-problem sends and shows the 'Sent to your Crew Lead and the owner.' toast without changing job status (En Route → En Route confirmed). Owner viewing the Stage2 Tester profile shows the full Work record (jobs, position chips, hours-pending, Crew Lead docs X/Y, and Timekeeping history flags). Tester viewing OWN profile also shows Work record. Helper viewing Tester's profile correctly HIDES work-record-section and profile-stats-block. Crew hitting /dispatch is redirected to /today (owner-only board). Backend network responses observed: POST /api/reliability/flags/{id}/resolve → 200, POST /api/crew/my-flags/{id}/dispute → 200, POST /api/crew/jobs/{id}/report-problem → 200, and GET /api/dispatch/board refreshes cleanly.

minor.issue: Resolving a possible_no_show 'unverified' flag while the underlying condition (no clock-in) still holds causes the next board fetch to immediately re-create a NEW unverified possible_no_show flag for the same user+assignment (different _id). The dispatch Reliability panel count therefore does not appear to decrease when the specific flag type resolved is possible_no_show/unverified. The resolve itself succeeds (POST returns 200, toast shows, the resolved doc is preserved for the Work record history), and other flag types (missing_clock_out, late_clock_in) DO decrement the panel and clear the crew flag badge as expected. Suggested fix: after resolve, either dedup against status='resolved' as well within the same day, or mark the assignment+user+type as 'suppressed until next event' so the scan doesn't immediately re-open it.

action_items: Investigate _scan_no_shows regenerating possible_no_show flags immediately after resolve (only impacts UX for that specific flag type — Reliability panel count does not decrease even though the resolve was recorded). Not a blocker for the Stage 3 acceptance criteria of the other flag types.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is still >12k lines (12119). Stage 3 reliability endpoints and _scan_no_shows are natural candidates to extract into a reliability_router module along with Stage 2 crew-lead endpoints.

_create_reliability_flag dedup only skips when an existing flag is in status open/unverified — combined with _scan_no_shows running on every /api/dispatch/board GET, a possible_no_show flag re-materializes right after resolve. Consider adding 'suppress-until-next-event' logic or including 'resolved' in the dedup window for the same day.

rca of the issue: Reliability panel count does not decrease when resolving a possible_no_show 'unverified' flag: at server.py:6828 the dispatch/board handler calls await _scan_no_shows(day) BEFORE returning the reliability list. _scan_no_shows() iterates every crew member scheduled today, and if the member still has no clock-in by arrival+grace it calls _create_reliability_flag(status='unverified'). _create_reliability_flag dedups only against existing docs whose status is in ['open','unverified'] (server.py:7797) — a just-resolved flag has status='resolved', so the dedup misses and a brand-new possible_no_show flag is inserted with a new _id. Net effect: the freshly resolved flag disappears from the panel, but on the very next 60s poll (or immediate refresh) an identical-looking replacement takes its slot. Mitigation options: (1) include 'resolved' in the dedup filter for same job_date, or (2) skip _scan_no_shows re-creation for {assignment_id,user_id,type} that already has a resolved flag today, or (3) short-circuit the scan when a resolved twin exists. Repro: log in as owner → /dispatch → click Resolve on a possible_no_show unverified flag → submit reason ≥3 chars → toast 'Flag resolved.' shows and dialog closes, but the panel count stays the same and a new flag id appears in place of the old one.
